title: Unit Econ pipeline design notes (stream vs batch, partitions, late events, cardinality)
content:
Last updated: 2025-02-11 (Mei)

Context
- We’re building the internal “unit economics” dashboard. The core metric is blended cost as $/1M output tokens with drilldowns by model, region, and customer tier.
- This doc is engineering design notes (not a PRD). It’s meant to capture pipeline approach options, partition strategy, late-event handling, and how we keep cardinality + query latency under control.
- Canonical metric definition is in ADR-0142 (source of truth). This doc focuses on implementation choices.

Primary goals (engineering)
1) Produce a daily dataset that powers dashboard + Finance tie-outs:
   - blended_cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens
   - plus key supporting measures (tokens, request counts, cache hit, effective throughput-ish proxies) to explain deltas.
2) Make late-arriving telemetry safe:
   - explicit watermarks, predictable backfill behavior, and “finalization” semantics.
3) Control dimensionality:
   - the dashboard can’t become a free-form OLAP cube over raw request logs.
4) Reconcile to billing/metering within agreed tolerance:
   - build a reconciliation job + alerting (ENG-2914) and keep “why variance” debuggable.

Non-goals (for phase 1)
- Per-request cost attribution exposed to the dashboard (too high cardinality + privacy risks). We can retain request-level data in restricted tables for debugging only.
- Real-time (sub-minute) unit cost. “Daily with near-real-time preview” is sufficient for weekly review cadence.
- Fully customer-facing unit economics. Internal-first.

High-level data flow (proposed)
Telemetry + cost inputs -> normalized fact tables -> daily aggregate -> semantic views -> dashboard API

Inputs (current understanding)
A) Metering / inference telemetry (streaming)
- Source: metering events from inference gateway + runtime (Kafka / event bus).
- Key fields: timestamp, request_id, account_id, region, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, route/runtime_config tags, quantization_profile tag, cache metrics (hit/miss + estimated saved tokens) once plumbed.
- Quality: duplicates possible; late arrivals common (client retries, delayed flush, partition lag).

B) Fleet compute cost inputs (batch)
- Source: daily fleet cost export (Vanessa Ortiz owns inputs).
- Grain (target): region x gpu_type x day, plus optional cluster/pool identifiers for dedicated.
- Includes: GPU cost, CPU/overhead components, reserved capacity amortization, and shared overhead allocation factor(s).

C) Mapping dimensions (slowly changing)
- Tier mapping: account_id -> tier (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise) with historical correctness (ENG-2911).
- Region mapping normalization: telemetry region codes -> finance region codes (fixes eu-west vs eu-west-1 style issues).
- Model mapping: model_id -> model_family + model_variant (stable names for dashboard).


Pipeline options considered

Option 1: Pure streaming (compute aggregates continuously)
- How: stream processor builds daily aggregates in near real-time; upserts per dimension bucket.
- Pros:
  - freshest possible numbers
  - naturally supports “today” charts
- Cons:
  - hard to make reconciliation deterministic (late-arrival + out-of-order)
  - upserts/compaction complexity, especially if we store aggregates in warehouse
  - complicated backfill story (replay a day/week)
- Verdict: not worth it for v1. Too hard to make Finance comfortable.

Option 2: Micro-batch for “preview” + daily batch for “official” (recommended)
- How:
  - Ingest raw metering events continuously into a warehouse staging table (append-only).
  - Hourly micro-batch builds “preview” aggregates for current day (marked as not-final).
  - Daily batch (T+1) builds official aggregates for day D, with controlled reprocessing window for late events (e.g., D-2..D).
- Pros:
  - deterministic daily numbers for Finance
  - still provides near-real-time directional visibility
  - straightforward backfill: rerun day partitions
  - warehouse-friendly (mostly append + MERGE for the last N days)
- Cons:
  - more moving parts (preview vs official)
  - we must clearly label “finalized” vs “subject to change”
- Verdict: best trade-off.

Option 3: Daily-only batch (no preview)
- Pros: simplest
- Cons: product/eng loses ability to catch regressions within the day; SRE prefers earlier signals
- Verdict: acceptable fallback if micro-batch becomes a distraction, but try to keep preview.


Recommended approach (Option 2 details)

Tables / datasets (names illustrative)
1) analytics.metering_events_raw (append-only)
- Partition: event_date (derived from event timestamp in UTC) + ingestion_date (for debugging)
- Dedup key: event_id if present; else (request_id, seq_no, event_type) with a time window
- Retention: raw events 90 days in analytics; longer retention in archive bucket

2) analytics.metering_events_normalized
- Normalized region codes, normalized model identifiers, joined tier mapping (as-of time), canonical token fields.
- Adds: quantization_profile, runtime_config_id (normalized), cache_* fields.
- Partition: event_date
- Note: This is where we enforce “allowed dimensions” and drop/transform high-cardinality fields.

3) analytics.unit_econ_daily_preview
- Grain: day x region x tier x model_variant x quantization_profile_bucket x runtime_config_bucket
- Populated hourly for current day (and maybe yesterday).
- Columns include: output_tokens, input_tokens, request_count, compute_cost_usd_est, overhead_cost_usd_est, blended_cost_usd_est, blended_cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens
- flagged is_final = false

4) analytics.unit_econ_daily (official)
- Same grain as preview.
- Written once per day for D-1, with a controlled reprocess window for late data (see Late events section).
- flagged is_final = true + finalized_at timestamp

5) analytics.unit_econ_reconciliation_daily
- Grain: day x region x tier
- Compares:
  - (a) unit_econ_daily totals rolled up
  - (b) billing/metering totals (from billing hooks) for the same slice
- Stores variance_pct + notes + links to investigation query templates


Metric computation notes (high level, ADR-0142 rules apply)
- Numerator components (USD):
  - compute_cost_usd: allocated GPU/fleet cost to usage based on a driver (tokens_out is the default for v1; revisit if we move to time-based allocation)
  - overhead_alloc_usd: shared platform overhead allocation per Finance methodology (can be % uplift or separate pool)
  - cache_savings_usd (if we model it explicitly): track savings as an explanatory measure; do not double-count (need clarity from ADR; early leaning is to reflect cache as reduced compute driver rather than subtracting a “savings” line item)
- Denominator: total output_tokens
- $/1M output tokens = (total_blended_cost_usd / total_output_tokens) * 1,000,000

Key implementation guardrail: keep numerator explainable.
- Store intermediate measures (compute_cost_usd, overhead_alloc_usd, discounts/credits excluded flag, etc.) so Finance can audit.


Partition strategy + clustering

Partitioning choices (warehouse)
- unit_econ_daily
  - Partition by: day (UTC date)
  - Cluster/sort by: region, tier, model_variant (and possibly quantization_profile_bucket)
  - Rationale:
    - Almost every dashboard query filters by date range + 1–3 of these dimensions.
    - Daily partitions align with Finance reporting + backfills.

Preview table
- Partition by: day
- We should keep preview retention short (e.g., 7–14 days) to avoid confusion and storage cost.

Raw/normalized events
- Partition by: event_date
- Additional ingestion_date partition helps debug “late event storms” and pipeline delays.

Timezones
- Canonical reporting day is UTC.
- If Finance wants a different “business day,” handle in the semantic layer, not in the storage partitioning.


Late-event handling

Definitions
- event_time: when inference happened (from runtime/gateway)
- ingest_time: when we received the event

Assumptions
- Typical lateness: < 2 hours
- Long tail lateness: up to 48 hours (observed during incidents and partial outages)
- Rare cases: > 72 hours (should be treated as exceptions)

Policy (v1 proposal)
- “Official” unit_econ_daily is computed T+1 and remains mutable for N days via reprocessing.
- Reprocessing window: last 3 days (D-2, D-1, D)
  - Daily job recomputes these partitions deterministically from normalized events.
  - After day D+3, mark partitions as frozen unless a manual backfill is approved.

Why 3 days?
- Enough to capture 48-hour lateness + provide buffer.
- Keeps compute cost of reruns bounded.

Mechanics
- Use an idempotent build pattern:
  - For each day in [today-2, today-1, today], recompute aggregates and MERGE/overwrite that partition.
- Track watermark stats per day:
  - pct_events_arrived_within_2h / 24h / 48h
  - late_event_count
- Surface this in data quality checks (SRE wants alerts when late-event rate spikes).

Dashboard semantics
- Show “Final” vs “Preliminary” labeling in UI.
- For date ranges that include non-final days, the top-level KPI should show a small “data may change” banner.

Manual backfills
- If a bug fix or missing data requires backfill (ENG-2918), use a runbooked job:
  - specify date range
  - dry-run mode that reports expected deltas
  - capture a backfill record: who/why/what changed


Cardinality constraints (this is the make-or-break)

Supported drilldown dimensions (v1)
- day
- region (normalized to a small set; no per-AZ)
- customer_tier (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise)
- model_variant (curated set; older/deprecated models mapped to “other/deprecated” bucket after a cutoff)
- quantization_profile_bucket
  - bucket into: fp16/bf16, int8, int4, other/unknown
  - keep the raw profile string in a restricted debug table only
- runtime_config_bucket
  - instead of storing arbitrary JSON, compute a stable “config hash” and map top K configs per model to human-readable labels
  - everything else -> “other”

Explicitly NOT supported in aggregate tables
- account_id / customer name
- request_id
- prompt hash / user-provided metadata
- per-route arbitrary tags

Guardrails
- Hard cap per day on distinct (model_variant, quant_profile_bucket, runtime_config_bucket) combinations written to unit_econ_daily.
  - Example: if runtime_config_bucket explodes, force to “other” beyond top K by volume.
- Maintain a “dimension cardinality report” emitted daily:
  - distinct counts per dimension
  - top N offenders (configs with small traffic but high count)
- Query guardrails for dashboard API (ENG-2919):
  - reject requests that attempt to filter on unsupported dimensions
  - enforce max date range for high-cardinality slices
  - cache results for common queries

Thomas Baird note (from Slack thread 1706201842):
- We should treat quant_profile and runtime_config as “explainers,” not as first-class dimensions for every chart. The default dashboard should prioritize model/region/tier and only expose deeper config slices behind an “Advanced” toggle.


Reconciliation notes
- Reconciliation should be computed on the SAME grain Finance cares about (day x region x tier) even if dashboard supports more drilldowns.
- Store reconciliation inputs alongside results:
  - unit_econ_total_usd
  - billing_metered_total_usd
  - variance_usd, variance_pct
  - token totals on both sides (where available)
- If variance exceeds threshold, attach “likely causes” tags:
  - region mapping mismatch
  - tier mapping lag
  - late events / incomplete partition
  - excluded credits/discounts mismatch
  - duplicate events spike
- This is both an alerting mechanism and a debugging index.


Operational considerations

Data quality checks (SRE)
- Freshness: latest event_date ingested within X minutes; latest unit_econ_daily updated by T+1 09:00 UTC
- Completeness: compare normalized token totals to raw within tolerance; monitor drop rates from normalization
- Late event rate: alert when > baseline
- Reconciliation variance: alert when > threshold (ENG-2914)

Ownership
- Ingestion + normalized events: Nadia Rahman
- Daily aggregates + partition reruns: Mei Lin
- Cardinality + query performance: Thomas Baird / Felix Schneider
- Reconciliation job: Cole Summers
- Alerts + SLO wiring: Allison Grant / Aisha Bello

Access controls
- unit_econ_daily is safe for broad internal (no customer identifiers).
- Anything with account_id joins (even for tier debugging) must be restricted and audited.


Open questions
1) Allocation driver: tokens_out vs tokens_total vs time-on-GPU proxy
   - tokens_out is simplest and aligns with “$/1M output tokens,” but may bias models with different input/output ratios.
   - Action: sync with Logan + Finance (Rishi) on whether we store both tokens_out and tokens_total allocs as separate measures.

2) Cache accounting
   - Do we reduce compute allocation driver by “effective tokens served from cache,” or do we show cache_savings_usd separately?
   - Need to avoid “negative costs” confusion and double counting.
   - Action: align with ADR-0142 interpretation and what the dashboard “Explain” panel expects.

3) Dedicated + Private cost attribution
   - Dedicated: can allocate using reserved capacity cost directly to that tier’s usage, but need a consistent methodology across pools.
   - Private/on-prem: may require separate cost inputs; likely out of v1.

4) Region normalization
   - What is the canonical set? (e.g., us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast)
   - Action: finalize mapping table and ensure billing uses the same.


Next steps (2-week plan)
- [ENG-2910] Lock unit_econ_daily schema + allowed dimension set; document in dataset dictionary.
- [ENG-2919] Implement runtime_config_bucket + quant_profile_bucket logic with top-K rollup.
- [ENG-2914] Stand up reconciliation job and wire basic alerting.
- Validate late-event window assumption with 30-day sample and propose final “freeze after N days” policy.

Appendix: quick “rules of thumb”
- If a dimension can be “unique per request,” it does NOT belong in the aggregate table.
- Prefer deterministic reruns over incremental “fixups” when late events arrive.
- Everything Finance will ask about should be stored as an explicit column (don’t hide logic in code only).
